In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanisms by which the vascular bed contributes to the etiology of elevated BP in the SHR and the DS rat.
the elucidation of mechanisms which may be responsible for the etiology of genetic hypertension.
the etiology and pathogenesis of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
altered vascular smooth muscle functions are not the cause of the elevated BP of the SHR and DS rats.
altered smooth muscle function may be a secondary phenomenon in the development of hypertension and that it is not the cause.
the role of altered smooth muscular function in hypertension is not entirely clear and further studies are required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alterations in smooth muscle function in hypertension are not a cause but rather a consequence of the hypertensive process.
the role of altered vascular reactivity in hypertension is not as great as previously thought and that genetic differences between strains are a major factor in the development of the hypertension.
the etiology of the high BP of the SHR and DS rats does not appear to be related to alterations in postsynaptics sensitivity or U1 activity, but rather to an altered renal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SHR and DS rats are not good models for studying altered smooth muscle function and its role in the development of hypertension.
altered vascular smooth muscle reactivity is not a primary factor in the etiology or maintenance of hypertension in the rat.

in vivo and in vitro studies are complementary and that the results obtained from both types of experiments must be considered when attempting to understand the etiology of the elevated BP in the SHR or DS rats.
